newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: INSTANT VIEW-Malaysia posts trade surplus in Feb.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-Malaysia posts trade surplus in Feb.

text.p: Following are views of economists on Malaysia's report of a trade surplus of 367.2 million ringgit in February:
KEVIN CHEW, ECONOMIST AT CASPIAN SECURITIES:
"February is usually a deficit because of seasonality (Chinese New Year/Eid al-Fitr) festivals, so this will be taken as a positive. But whether it is sustainable is questionable.
(National airline) MAS is taking delivery of planes and (shipping firm) MISC is importing ships.
It's a matter of magnitude of how much it will worsen. The central bank has also put in the assumption for its recent forecast.
But the (stock) market is so bad you can't do anything to it."
"The surplus of 367 million ringgit for February's trade is undoubtedly good news but it is just a notch above what the market has factored in, i.e. a small deficit to surplus of 300 million ringgit.
Risk is in fact for some 'selling (ringgit) on facts'.
Further out, the market will start to focus on how the balance will fare once the new (airline) MAS Boeings are taken into account come April.
MUSTAFA MOHD NOR, CHIEF ECONOMIST ARAB MALAYSIAN SECURITIES:

"The market was expecting a deficit not a surplus, so it's a surprise. It is quite consistent with previous years when exports and imports slowed down in February, partly because of (Chinese and Moslem) festivals and the shorter month.

"But the figures also show that the trend towards private capital formation is still not picking, as indicated in a jump in capital imports. The market is actually looking for a higher import figure as an indication that private capital formation is picking up and growth is being sustained.
"March numbers from Singapore are also showing this weak trend."
